cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Put It Back Quietly
cards.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your umbrella is back in the stand. Handle up, please; we store it so you can take it straight to work.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is it wet? It hasn't rained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Routine cleaning. The fabric needs rinsing before the handle is dried; those are separate jobs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we remove debris before closing it. Please hold the stand; I'll rinse it again and put it back correctly this time.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 storage orientation, A3 cleaning sequence and A5 debris removal use professional maintenance to conceal why the umbrella is being restored.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 wet-without-rain causes A3 cleaning cover; B4 pondweed causes A5 another rinse, but holding the stand has no evident purpose.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 question B own object condition and supply increasingly revealing evidence.

heightening.evidence: A5 treats B4 pondweed as unfinished maintenance rather than explain its origin.

specificity.evidence: A1 umbrella returned for work is legible; A5 stand-holding invites an unnecessary staging problem.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 separate jobs is somewhat explanatory, and A5 can ask for a useful restoration aid instead of stand support.

coach2.situation: A1 umbrella returned for work is legible; A5 stand-holding invites an unnecessary staging problem.
coach2.stated: A1 umbrella in stand; B2 no rain; B4 pondweed in spokes; A5 rinse again without explaining origin.
coach2.inferred: A is hiding prior misuse by acting as the qualified restorer.
coach2.missing: The stand does not need to be held for the stated rinse, so that request lacks practical grounding.
coach2.firstDefect: A5 asks B to hold the stand without a stated reason.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 questions wetness of A1 returned umbrella.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 supplies a maintenance explanation for B2 wetness.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 names revealing debris despite A3 routine-cleaning claim.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 turns B4 debris into more rinsing but gives B an unmotivated stand task.
